# Rules Catalog

| ID | Title | Area | Strength | Class | Instruction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RULE-001 | Own the application shell as an application composition | app-shell | should | convention | Compose the whole application inside a FluentProvider and build the shell navigation yourself from Nav, Toolbar, and layout primitives, because v9 exports no shell component. |
| RULE-002 | Use Nav for the primary hierarchy and Breadcrumb for position | app-shell | should | recommendation | Render the primary destinations with Nav and its item parts, and render the current position with Breadcrumb, because routing itself stays application-owned. |
| RULE-003 | Give each page one heading that names its task | page-chrome | must | requirement | Place a single top-level heading that names the screen's task at the start of the content region, and use lower heading levels only for structure beneath it. |
| RULE-004 | Keep one primary action and move the rest into a toolbar | page-chrome | should | recommendation | Reserve one visually primary action for the screen and place additional page commands in a Toolbar, moving overflow actions into a menu. |
| RULE-005 | Bind every input to a visible label and helper text | forms | must | requirement | Wrap each control in a Field that provides a visible label, and place help or error text through the Field's message slot rather than beside it. |
| RULE-006 | Validate on blur and submit, and after the user has entered a value | forms | should | recommendation | Show a field error after the user leaves the field or submits the form, and never before the user has entered a value, so the form does not scold an untouched field. |
| RULE-007 | Default forms to a single column and group related fields | forms | should | recommendation | Lay fields out in one column by default and group related fields under a shared heading, because a single reading path is easier to follow and to complete. |
| RULE-008 | Use a dialog for a short, focused decision | overlays | should | recommendation | Place a short, self-contained decision in a Dialog with a title and explicit action buttons, so the interaction stays bounded and easy to dismiss. |
| RULE-009 | Prefer a drawer over a dialog for a longer contextual edit | overlays | should | recommendation | Use a Drawer for a contextual edit that keeps the underlying context visible, and confirm before discarding unsaved changes when the drawer closes. |
| RULE-010 | Choose DataGrid when columns control layout and Table when the DOM table matters | data-grid | should | recommendation | Use DataGrid when the layout must be controlled by column definitions and keyboard grid behavior is required, and use Table when a native table structure is the goal. |
| RULE-011 | State whether sorting, filtering, and paging run locally or on the server | data-grid | should | convention | Decide explicitly whether each collection operation runs on loaded rows or on the server, and pass the resulting state into the grid so the component does not imply a data source it does not have. |
| RULE-012 | State whether a selection applies to loaded rows or to all matching results | data-grid | must | requirement | Make the selection scope explicit to the user, and when a bulk action can apply to all matching results rather than only the loaded page, offer that choice deliberately. |
| RULE-013 | Do not hide task-required fields inside a collapsed section | disclosure | must | requirement | Keep fields that the task requires visible or clearly summarized, and reserve collapsed sections for genuinely optional or advanced content. |
| RULE-014 | Use tabs for peer views and not for sequential steps | disclosure | should | recommendation | Use TabList to switch between peer views of the same record, and keep sequential task steps out of tabs so users are not misled about order. |
| RULE-015 | Choose persistence by urgency: MessageBar for durable, Toast for transient | feedback | should | recommendation | Place conditions the user must be able to read later in a MessageBar, and place short-lived confirmations in a Toast, because the two differ in persistence and urgency. |
| RULE-016 | Design explicit loading, empty, search-empty, and error states | feedback | must | requirement | Provide a distinct state for loading, for genuinely empty data, for an empty search result, and for a failed load, so the user can tell the difference and knows what to do next. |
| RULE-017 | Style through the two-layer token model, not hard-coded values | theming | must | requirement | Reference Fluent tokens through makeStyles instead of hard-coding colors, spacing, or font values, so a theme change flows through the whole app. |
| RULE-018 | Use the type ramp instead of ad-hoc font sizes | theming | should | convention | Assign text a role from the Fluent type ramp and let the role determine size, weight, and line height, rather than setting font sizes per screen. |
| RULE-019 | Respect reduced motion and keep motion purposeful | theming | must | requirement | Honor the user's reduced-motion preference and keep transitions short and purposeful, because motion that cannot be suppressed can cause discomfort. |
| RULE-020 | Keep focus visible and never obscure the focused control | accessibility | must | requirement | Preserve a visible focus indicator on every interactive element and ensure sticky or overlaying regions never cover the focused control. |
| RULE-021 | Follow the composite-widget keyboard model for grids, menus, and tabs | accessibility | must | requirement | Give composite widgets a single tab stop and arrow-key movement within it, and ensure nested action controls are reachable without conflicting with row activation. |
| RULE-022 | Provide names, roles, and instructions for non-text content | accessibility | must | requirement | Give every meaningful icon or color-coded control a programmatic name and an instruction where needed, and hide purely decorative icons from assistive technology. |
| RULE-023 | Reflow content rather than shrinking it | responsive | must | requirement | Let content reflow into a single column and scroll vertically so nothing is lost, rather than clipping or forcing two-dimensional scrolling. |
| RULE-024 | Use logical properties so layouts mirror under RTL | responsive | should | convention | Express margins, padding, and alignment with logical properties and set the provider direction, so the layout mirrors without a separate stylesheet. |
| RULE-025 | Plan for long content and truncation with an accessible full value | responsive | should | recommendation | Let long values wrap where space allows and truncate with an accessible full value where it does not, so hidden text stays available. |
| RULE-026 | Provide one root FluentProvider with an explicit theme and direction | composition | must | requirement | Wrap the application in a single FluentProvider that sets the theme and text direction, and let nested providers be exceptions rather than the rule. |
| RULE-027 | Keep application state in the application, not in Fluent | composition | must | requirement | Own routing, data fetching, authorization, and persistence in application code, and use Fluent components only for presentation and local interaction state. |
| RULE-028 | Compose with makeStyles and slots instead of wrapping Fluent internals | composition | should | convention | Style Fluent components with makeStyles and compose their public slots, rather than depending on internal class names or undocumented DOM structure. |
| RULE-029 | Guard unsaved changes before they can be lost | task-flows | must | requirement | Track dirty state and confirm before discarding unsaved changes when the user closes, navigates away from, or switches context in the editor. |
| RULE-030 | Prevent duplicate submission and show pending work | task-flows | must | requirement | Disable the submit action while a request is pending, show progress in place, and re-enable the action when the request settles. |
| RULE-031 | Give every sortable column a compare function | data-grid | must | requirement | Provide a compare function in every column definition whose header is meant to sort; a column without compare stays unsortable even when the grid enables sorting. |
| RULE-032 | Set a cell focus mode when the cell contains interactive controls | data-grid | must | requirement | Set focusMode group on a cell with several focusable elements so Enter enters the cell and Escape returns to it, and set focusMode none on a cell with exactly one focusable element so that control receives focus directly. |
| RULE-033 | Do not nest focusable controls inside a sortable header cell | data-grid | must | requirement | Keep a sortable header cell free of nested focusable controls; move header actions into a context menu or into the body cells instead. |
| RULE-034 | Treat column resizing as a preview capability with an explicit overflow container | data-grid | should | recommendation | Use resizableColumns only inside a container that allows horizontal overflow, provide the column sizing options, and keep keyboard resizing available; do not let resizing push the page into two-dimensional scrolling. |
| RULE-035 | Memoize the row render function before virtualizing a grid | data-grid | must | requirement | Keep the row render function stable with useCallback and a stable row key before enabling virtualization, and virtualize only after measuring a performance need. |
| RULE-036 | Give selection controls a descriptive accessible name | data-grid | must | requirement | Provide an aria-label through the selection cell for both the header select-all control and each row control, naming the action and, for the header, the selection scope. |
